turn1.explanation: The unit fires on clause- and sentence-ending punctuation (commas, periods, semicolons) in documents that have a ship, boat or nautical context, apparently carrying that topic forward at each boundary. It does not fire on the nautical words themselves.
turn1.evidence: Nearly every high-activation window is about boats or ships (the SeaArk jon boats at up to 4.19, power ships, a cruise-ship casino, Sweden's listed ships, flying boats, V.Ships), and even the outliers contain 'anchor' (Anchor Electronics, 'anchor matter content'). In all of them the activation sits on , . ; and words like 'boat' or 'ship' score only about 0.1; the weaker mid-range examples also involve ships (Stargate vessel, pirate ship, sunken rig, cargo ship), except the medical and news-broadcasting texts.
turn1.missing_data: Activations on punctuation in long non-maritime documents, compared with maritime text that has little punctuation, would show whether the topic gate is real or the unit is mainly a generic list/clause punctuation detector.
